source.title: Linear Probes Transfer from Base to Distilled Language Models despite Rotation

page_placements.theme: Training origins: harm discrimination predates alignment; post-training creates or amplifies a refusal gate shaped by the objective

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a harmful-versus-safe mean-difference direction and a base-trained probe transfer across distilled and instruction-tuned model variants. It extends the transfer question to these successor types, but measures label separation rather than model refusal behavior.
record.gate_note: The study defines its direction from unsafe minus safe prompt activations and labels prompts by what a well-calibrated model should refuse. It explicitly says it measures no model behavior and runs no causal test. Thus it does not test refusal mediation, ablation, addition, weight edits, or whether attacks suppress a refusal direction. Its probe-transfer and direction-rotation results bear on V6 as representational transfer, not on refusal rates. The paper also reports control-direction rotations, but these are not results on the safety direction itself.
record.test_reason: It builds an unsafe-minus-safe mean-difference direction and linear probes, but labels are XSTest/OR-Bench safe/unsafe annotations, not model refusals. The authors state they measure no model behaviour and run no causal test. Probe AUC transfer and direction rotation measure a harmfulness-label representation, not whether a refusal-mediating direction carries across variants. Arditi et al. is cited only as related work. No version is tested; findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Base-trained harmful-request probes kept similar observed AUC on distilled and instruction-tuned successors in four families, despite up to 35° rotation. Their advantage over text cues is clear on XSTest and only partial on OR-Bench. No model behaviour or causal test.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an unsafe-minus-safe mean-activation direction and trained linear probes, but evaluates classification transfer and direction rotation rather than ablating or adding a refusal direction and measuring refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected layer varies by fold; the authors also report a fixed-layer check with a similar XSTest transfer picture. Performance and probe-versus-text margins differ between XSTest and OR-Bench.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-trained unsafe-vs-safe probes applied unchanged to R1-distilled and instruct successors keep AUC (XSTest change −0.011 to +0.027; OR-Bench −0.015 to +0.053), though the mean-difference direction rotates 17°–35°. Control directions rotate comparably.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear harmfulness-label probes and mean-difference directions trained on base models transfer to distilled and instruct successors despite direction rotation.

fits_no_version.finding: Probes beat a text-only classifier by 0.15–0.20 AUC on XSTest but only 0.03–0.20 on OR-Bench. At default threshold they flag 29%–42% of benign OR-Bench hard prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness probes partly read surface appearance of harm; their advantage over text cues depends on the evaluation set.

record.problems: The authors state that they measure no model behavior and run no causal test. XSTest fold intervals are nominal and too narrow because folds share training groups. There are four related model families, one distillation recipe, and the independent labels are OR-Bench's operational moderation labels rather than an independent ground truth. Instruction-tuned models are evaluated on raw prompts outside their chat format.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. The paper's control-direction rotation comparisons are described in Section 5.2 and Figure B.2 but are not rows because they measure directions built from labels unrelated to safety, not the claimed safety/refusal direction.

untested.parts: No ablation, addition, or refusal measurement.
No multi-direction or cone analysis of refusal.
Harmfulness labels probed, but refusal decision never measured, so no separation test.
No refusal behaviour or causal role checked in successors; only label-probe transfer.
No link between training method and a removable refusal direction.
Distilled reasoning models included, but no refusal mediation tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 supports/limits_scope labels are removed: the label is what a model 'should refuse', not what it does. Other unrecorded results also bear on no version: control-direction rotations (Fig. B.2), fixed-layer check (Table B.3), and preliminary RL checkpoints (cosine ≥0.999, Appendix C).

versions.untested_parts: No causal ablation or addition and no measurement of refusal behavior or preserved capabilities.
No weight edit or evaluation of released-model refusal behavior after an edit.
No jailbreak attack suppressing the direction and no training against its ablation.
No test comparing an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
No comparison of harmfulness judgment with a refusal decision.

Tests transfer of harmful-versus-safe prompt classification and direction across four model families to distilled and instruction-tuned successors. It does not test refusal behavior, transfer across languages, or other model families and training recipes.
Compares successor types for representation transfer, but does not test how refusal training determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.
Includes distilled reasoning models but does not test whether a refusal direction mediates their refusal behavior.

unmatched_labels.label: none
unmatched_labels.reason: No version is tested. The rows measure safety-label probe AUC and the rotation of a label direction, with no refusal rate and no ablation or addition (Limitations section). The direction is a related construct, so the finding fits_no_version.

relation.reason: Arditi et al. is cited twice: once as an example of probes, and once in related work as concerning refusal behaviour 'which we do not measure'. 'discusses' would also be defensible, but there is no engagement beyond that.

tranche.reason: The safety direction is a safety-label difference-in-means on XSTest (base-model prompts, raw text). The authors state they measure no model behaviour and run no causal test, so they test neither refusal mediation nor refusal-direction transfer, and they do not use the refusal direction as a tool.

source_check.notes: The r11 row note is wrong: the second distilled OR-Bench interval excluding zero is qwen-32b, not math-7b. The authors_conclusion and test_reason are accurate. The safety direction uses the last 8 tokens of raw-text prompts with no chat template, unlike Arditi's chat-formatted post-instruction positions, so it should not be read as a refusal direction for V6.

statements.correction: Controls (38 directions) were compared only under distillation: safety direction rotates 30.5-35.1 deg, comparable to the controls, and prompt length rotates more in every family. Instruct rotations (17.1-33.6 deg) had no control comparison. Authors call AUC 'similar observed accuracy, not demonstrated equivalence'. On OR-Bench, llama-8b distilled (+0.042) and qwen-32b distilled (-0.015) intervals exclude zero; all instruct OR-Bench changes are gains.
statements.problem: All numbers match: XSTest -0.011 to +0.027, OR-Bench -0.015 to +0.053, rotation 17-35 deg. But the paper reports the control-direction comparison only under distillation. The statement implies it also covers instruct rotations.
